definition: Percy Liang is an American computer scientist whose research focuses on machine learning, natural language processing, and foundation models.
details: Coined and formalized the paradigm of 'Foundation Models', created the Holistic Evaluation of Language Models (HELM), and co-founded Together AI. He is a Professor of Computer Science at Stanford University and is the Director of the Center for Research on Foundation Models (CRFM).

explainer.lead: Percy Liang is an American computer scientist. His work spans computer science.
explainer.knownFor: Liang is known for his work on semantic parsing, weak and indirect supervision, robustness and generalization in machine learning, and the study of large-scale foundation models.

contributions.name: Liang has authored peer-reviewed publications in artificial intelligence and machine learning venues, including ACL, EMNLP, ICML, and COLT.

timeline.what: As a high school student in 1999, Liang participated in the Research Science Institute at MIT.
He competed twice for the U.S. team in the International Olympiad in Informatics (IOI), winning bronze in 1999 and silver in 2000.
Liang went on to serve as the team's deputy leader in 2003, 2006, and 2008.
Liang received a Bachelor of Science degree in 2004 and a Master of Engineering degree in 2005 from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology.
Doctor of Philosophy, University of California, Berkeley
Receives the Presidential Early Career Award for Scientists and Engineers
